contexts.text: In these numbers, five dominates, which, in the Word, = something, or a little, and a few. Illustrated. AC 798. AC 1429.
Five () = disunion, because it = a little.
Peradventure there shall lack five () = if there should be somewhat less. Five = a little, or less.
Wilt Thou destroy the whole city for five. () = shall man perish for the little that is lacking.
Five = a little... and also disjunction. AC 2269:2.
Five = somewhat that is little.
From before the rebuke of five shall ye flee (). Five = few.
For this hanging there were five pillars and five bases (), by which number is signified what is relatively little.

Five of them were prudent, and five were foolish = part of them who were in truths in which there is good, and part who were in truths in which there is no good... Five, in the internal sense, = some; here, therefore, part of them. AC 10253:end. DSS 17:2. AR 427:2. AE 187:4. AE 375:41. AE 548:3. AE 675:6.

Let him take a fifth of the land () = which are to be preserved and afterwards stored up. To take a fifth here involves the same as to tithe, which = remains... Ten = remains, and therefore so does five, which is the half of ten.

Five has a double signification. It = a little and thus somewhat, and it = remains. It = a little from its relation to those numbers which = much, namely, a thousand and a hundred, and thus also ten... which, from them, also = much... Five = remains when it has relation to ten, which = remains.
The servant who received five talents = those who have admitted goods and truths from the Lord, thus who have received remains.
Here, in like manner (), ten and five = remains; ten more, five fewer. Further illustrated. AC 5291:8. AC 5291:9. AC 5291:10.
Five multiplied into six = somewhat of combat; because five = somewhat...

By five measures () = much ind... Five is a number which = a little, also somewhat, and likewise much; its signification Hows from its relation to the number from which it originates. When it comes from ten, it involves what is similar, but in a less degree; for it is the half of ten... Five measures were given to Benjamin above the rest of his brethren... because ten could not be given, for ten would have been far too much.
There are five years yet () = the duration of this state until remains shine forth. Five = remains.
There are still five years of famine () = the duration of the lack of good.
And five changes of garments () = much of the truth which is from the Natural. Five = much.
On the part of his brethren he took five men () = some of the truths of the Church... Five = some.
Ye shall give the fifth part to Pharaoh () = remains, that they are for the general principle which is under the guidance of the Internal. Five, and the fifth part = remains. AC 6166.
Under Fifty, see this reference.
He shall repay five oxen for an ox; () = the corresponding penalty much. Five = somewhat, and also much. AE 548:7.
The reason two and a half = much and full, is that it has a like signification to five, ten, a hundred, a thousand; for the double of two and a half is five... That five = much and full. References.
Under Curtain, see this reference.
Five = all things of the one part; for ten = all things of the whole.
Five (staves) for the beams of one side of the habitation () = where it looks towards the interior things of Heaven, where truth is in light; (for) five = all things of that side. AC 9664.
Five pillars of shittim () = support so far as is sufficient by the good of merit... Five = some part, or something, and also as much as is sufficient.

Five cubits the length, and five cubits the breadth () = equally from good and from truth... The reason the length and the breadth of the altar were of five cubits, was that five also = the like with ten, a hundred, a thousand; and by these numbers is signified much, all, what is full, and, in the supreme sense, which treats of the Lord, what is infinite; so also does five. AC 10253.
The height five cubits () = degrees of good also so far as is sufficient.
The first state of man is from birth to the fifth year of his age... Illustrated.
When ten = all, five = some; when ten = what is full, five = as much as is sufficient; and when ten = much, five = somewhat.
Ten (in the parable of the pounds) = much, and five = some. AE 223:23. AE 548:4. AE 675:7.
To torment them five months () = to induce a stupor for a short time. Five = a little, or for a short time. Illustrated. AR 427:2. AR 439.
Five (kings) have fallen () = that all the Divine truths of the Word have been destroyed... By five is not signified five, but all the rest. Explained. (Compare AE 1064.)
Five cities in the land of Egypt speaking with the lip of Canaan () = truths of doctrine in abundance... Five = many or in abundance. AE 391:13. AE 654:7. (Compare AE 548:6.)

Five (as a simple number from which greater numbers derive their signification) = much and somewhat... From the number five arise 10, 50, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, which numbers have a like signification to five, because they arise from it by multiplication. AE 532.
Five () = a few.
Five, in the Word, = all these when two and three follow; but when five is preceded or followed by ten or twenty, it = some and a few.

Five months = so long as they remain in this state... For a month = a state; and five, somewhat, and therefore so long as... That five = somewhat, may appear from the passages in the Word where this number occurs; for the numbers 10, 1000, 10000, = much and all, and hence five = somewhat; for those numbers which = much arise from the number five, which = somewhat.
That five, in the Word, = somewhat and some, likewise all who are such, and other similar things. Illustrated.
Some, and all who are such, are signified by the five brethren (in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, ).
Five yoke of oxen () = all those affections or cupidities which lead away from Heaven.
The fifth part = as much as is sufficient. Illustrated.

To the fifth rib = as much as was sufficient for death. For the same number which = somewhat, and all that is on the one side, also = as much as is sufficient, when it is predicated of quantity; and so long as, when it is predicated of time.

As this number = somewhat, and all that is on one side, it also = a little and a few, when it is followed or preceded by a great quantity which is also designated by numbers; for in this case the whole that is on one side is relatively a little. Illustrated.
The reason five sparrows are mentioned (), is that five = what is small and of little value in comparison with man.
Ten = all things and all men; and five, one part, or one kind.
Five and ten (in the parable of the talents) = somewhat and much, thus that the first servant from some Knowledges of truth and good procured for himself much wisdom.
When five follows ten, it = some people or some things, likewise all the rest which remain, and also a few; but when it does not follow ten, it = many people or many things.
